newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares tick up, new issues dominate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares tick up, new issues dominate.

text.p: Singapore shares opened slightly firmer on Thursday with most attention and activity focused on new share issues.
Singapore's benchmark 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) stood at 2,041.77 by 0150 GMT, up 1.34.

Shares in property and steel company Lion Teck Chiang began their first day of trading at Singapore $1.30 each, level with the firm's initial public offer. They rose to a high of S$1.38 with 1.6 million shares changing hands in the first 50 minutes.
Two other recent issues took top volume: disk drive maker MMI Holdings and healthcare company Raffles Medical Group.
MMI, which debuted on Wednesday, rose six cents to S$0.60 on 10.4 million shares. Raffles Medical, which began trading last week, rose 2.5 cents to S$0.565 on 5.2 million shares.
Of the STII stocks, marine group SembCorp rose 15 cents to S$6.45 and car retailer Cycle & Carriage fell 20 cents to S$15.

Dealers said the index was benefiting from an overnight rise on Wall Street where the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 92.71 points to close at 6,679.87. They added that the market was likely to firm later on book-squaring ahead of a long weekend in Singapore. Friday is a public holiday.
